title: HELIX Bridge: Ellucian Colleague → AcademicPeriod
description: Maps Ellucian Colleague term data to the HELIX AcademicPeriod resource.

source_files.description: Term definition file. Contains term codes, descriptions, dates, and reporting year.
Session/part-of-term definitions within a term. Start/end dates, census dates for sub-terms.

attribute_mappings.transformation: Colleague term codes vary by institution but commonly follow patterns like '2026FA' (Fall 2026), '2027SP' (Spring 2027), '2026SU' (Summer 2026). Derive period type from term code pattern or TERMS.REPORTING.TERM field. Map to HELIX: semester, quarter, etc.
attribute_mappings.notes: Colleague term codes are less standardized than Banner's YYYYMM convention. Institution-specific mapping is often required.

attribute_mappings.transformation: Map to YYYY-YYYY format. Colleague may store as a single year ('2026'). Convert: '2026' → '2026-2027' based on institutional convention.
Convert Colleague date format (integer days since 12/31/1967) to ISO 8601
Convert Colleague date format to ISO 8601
Convert Colleague date format to ISO 8601. Use the full-term session census date if available.
attribute_mappings.notes: Census date may be stored at the term level or the session level depending on Colleague configuration.

attribute_mappings.transformation: true if current date is between start_date and end_date

special_considerations.description: Colleague stores all dates as integer values representing the number of days since December 31, 1967. This applies to ALL date fields across all files. Conversion formula: ISO_date = date(1967, 12, 31) + timedelta(days=colleague_int_value). Example: Colleague value 21275 = August 30, 2026. This conversion must be applied in every Bridge mapping that includes date fields.

Colleague's MV database stores repeating groups within a single record. For example, a student's multiple statuses over time are stored as a multi-valued field within a single STUDENTS record, not as separate rows. Bridge implementations must handle MV field parsing — typically exploding multi-valued fields into rows during extraction.
